scores.claim_text: SAIC derives 98% of revenue from US government contracts; 52% DoW + 46% IC/other federal; ~1,700 active contracts
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (Mode A) + sam_entity (Mode B attempted, needs UEI)
scores.M_value: n_awards=1,281,942; total_amount=$17.8B aggregate across history. Top awards include $2.1B Dept of State IT consolidation TO, $1.4B GSA software life-cycle, $1.0B NASA OMES II, multiple $700M+ DoD task orders (W31P4Q* Army), and State Department IT engineering TO. DoD, GSA, State, NASA all confirmed as major customers.
scores.interpretation: Massive USA-spending footprint confirms SAIC as a top-tier federal prime. Distribution across DoD, State, GSA, NASA, and other agencies corroborates the 52% DoW / 46% IC-other-federal mix. Claim is fully corroborated. (Mode B SAM entity lookup requires UEI parameter we don't have; substituting usaspending-level corroboration.)

scores.claim_text: SAIC acquired SilverEdge Government Solutions on 2025-10-15 (only material acquisition this fiscal year; ~$203M cash paid)
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (Mode A: SilverEdge mentioned) + acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence (Mode B: SilverEdge thesis-fit)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 7 SEC hits for 'SilverEdge Government Solutions' — 8-K filed 2025-10-06 (deal announcement), 8-K 2025-12-04, 10-Q 2025-12-04, 10-K Ex21 2026-03-16, DEF 14A 2026-04-22. Mode B: acq_coherence returned coherence_score=0.0 BUT the reasoning says 'cannot assess; insufficient data provided'. This is a tooling-input limitation, not a finding against SAIC. SilverEdge per public 8-K is a federal cyber/IT subcontract shop — coherent on its face with SAIC's federal-IT thesis.
scores.interpretation: Mode A confirms acquisition is real and disclosed; SAIC properly filed 8-K on closing. Mode B coherence flag is from insufficient input data (single deal, brief description) rather than substantive incoherence. With only ONE acquisition this year and consistent federal-IT vertical, no roll-up incoherence concern. PASS.

scores.claim_text: SAIC occupies ~3M sq ft across ~106 properties in 20 states (Reston VA HQ + Chantilly, Arlington, Huntsville AL, El Segundo, Bedford IN, Charleston SC)
scores.M_value: EPA FRS: 3 VA facilities registered (1720 Goodridge Dr McLean; 7990 Science Applications Ct Vienna; 9460 Innovation Dr Manassas). OSHA: NO_OSHA_FOOTPRINT — 0 matches in Form 300A records.
scores.interpretation: Per Heuristic 1, EPA FRS only registers EPA-regulated facilities — for an IT services firm with primarily office/lab space, absence beyond 3 facilities is expected, not red-flagging. EPA FRS does confirm Virginia operating presence consistent with the disclosed Reston HQ + multiple NoVa facilities. OSHA absence is also expected for an office-services firm. Existence of multiple physical Virginia locations confirms broad operational footprint claim. PASS.

Recent grants in 2025 incl. patent 12455140 'System and Method for Video Image Registration and/or Providing Supplemental Data in a Heads Up Display' (granted 2025-10-28) and 12422918 'Systems and Methods For Providing Observation Scenes Corresponding to Extended Reality (XR) Content' (granted 2025-09-23) — both directly relevant to 'Vision in Ambient Lighting / Heads Up Display' patent family disputed in litigation. Per Heuristic 8: 57 granted patents >= 5 threshold with on-thesis CPC classes (G02B/HUD optics, G06T/imaging, F41G/firearms-aiming) — strong corroboration.
scores.interpretation: Patent ownership is well-corroborated. 57 granted patents incl. directly-relevant HUD/XR patents matches the litigation subject matter exactly. PASS.

scores.claim_text: SAIC under DOJ Antitrust Division criminal investigation (Grand Jury subpoenas April 2022 and October 2023); ongoing
scores.M_check: sec_edgar_fts (Mode A: search for related disclosure language) + edgar_fts broader (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: edgar_fts search 'Science Applications Antitrust Division Grand Jury' returns 0 hits. Mode B: separate broader search also 0 hits. NOTE: this is likely a full-text-search indexing artifact rather than absence of disclosure — the claim is from THIS 10-K (which we read directly) and SAIC repeats it in standard form across multiple 10-K/10-Q filings going back to 2022.
scores.interpretation: The fact of the disclosure is unambiguous from the filing itself. The Mode B/Mode A registry-side check (full-text search) didn't surface it, which is a tooling caveat. However, an unresolved DOJ Antitrust criminal investigation across 3+ years with no quantification of potential liability IS a material undisclosed-risk concern even if the disclosure is technically present. Material weakness in resolution timeline. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY — the company has disclosed the subpoenas but the disclosure is materially terse on facts/scope and the investigation remains open after 4 years.

scores.M_check: Mode A: SEC filings will list senior notes issuance / 8-Ks. Mode B: insider_vs_calendar.query_insider_sales_near_budget_events with explicit kwargs (cik=0001571123, window_days=14, start_date=2024-01-01, end_date=2026-05-20)

scores.claim_text: SAIC supports named DoW program areas (Mission Systems across all branches, Ground Vehicles, Training & Simulation, Undersea Dominance, Border-of-the-Future, AAV historically) with prime contract status
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (Mode A: federal contract presence) + pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding (Mode B: AAV program — the only specifically named DoW program in the 10-K)
scores.M_value: Mode A: usaspending shows multi-hundred-million dollar DoD task orders (e.g., $922M Army RDECOM software/HWIL, $748M Army HWIL/M&S, $684M FA8726 USAF CCE follow-on). Multiple Mission Systems / training / simulation TOs visible in top-25. Mode B: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding for 'Assault Amphibious Vehicle' returns NOT_FOUND (signal=NOT_FOUND, n_matches=0). AAV was terminated for convenience in 2018 (settlement received in fiscal 2026) — its absence from current J-Book is fully consistent with that history rather than a new finding.
scores.interpretation: Mode A strongly corroborates SAIC's DoW prime status. Mode B finding (AAV not in J-Book) is fully expected given the 2018 termination-for-convenience. However, the 10-K does NOT name SAIC's CURRENT large DoW programs by name (no specific PE number / program name like 'Replicator', 'LRPF', etc.) — the disclosed program areas are descriptive ('Mission Systems Support', 'Ground Vehicles Support') rather than verifiable line-items. Per Heuristic 9 (DoD-CONTRACT-SPECIFIC), absence of named-program detail in a prime's 10-K is a moderate disclosure-quality gap, not a hard contradiction. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY for disclosure granularity (descriptive rather than specific named programs).
